name: Sterling-Nakamura Encrypted Document Scanner EDS-3
description: A handheld document scanner that photographs, OCRs, encrypts, and securely transmits paper documents to a designated secure server in a single operation. The EDS-3 is designed for intelligence gathering — an operator can scan a desk full of documents in under a minute, with each page automatically encrypted before leaving the device's memory. The scanner also detects and flags documents with embedded security features — watermarks, UV-reactive inks, tracking fibers — that could identify the source of a leak. Sterling-Nakamura's legal and intelligence teams use it for everything from corporate espionage to due diligence.

specifications.info: UV ink; tracking fiber identification; 000 pages internal encrypted

story_hooks: An EDS-3 captured in a corporate raid contained scans of 4,000 pages of classified documents — the metadata shows they were scanned over six months from a single office, identifying the leak source.

A modified EDS-3 has been developed that replaces scanned documents with altered versions — the operator scans the original, the device prints a modified copy, and the switch is made in the same operation.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, pistol-grip handheld scanner resembling a compact thermal imaging device. The form factor is aggressive and utilitarian—designed for rapid deployment in field conditions. Slight forward taper toward the optical head gives it a predatory appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: 18 cm long, 8 cm wide, 5 cm deep—roughly the size of a modern dental imaging tool
physical_description.weight_description: 150 grams; lightweight and pocketable with a wrist strap, designed for one-handed operation during rapid document sweeps
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer chassis with rubberized grip sections; anodized aluminum trim around the optical array
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with brushed aluminum accents; textured grip panels to prevent slipping during wet-work scenarios
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray body with crimson accent striping along the trigger guard and status indicator ring; silver-chrome optical lens housing
physical_description.interface_elements: Recessed touchscreen (2.1-inch OLED display) on dorsal surface showing live preview and encryption status; capacitive trigger button; micro-USB charging port hidden beneath a security clasp; three physical status LEDs (power, encryption, transmission) arranged vertically on the right flank
distinctive_features: Rotating optical head with integrated UV lamp array visible beneath translucent lens cap
Pulsing crimson LED ring that illuminates during active encryption—cyclic pattern indicates data scrambling in real-time
Laser targeting dot (non-visible to human eye but cast onto documents for alignment) creates subtle shimmering effect on paper
Subtle Sterling-Nakamura etched logo on grip: intertwined S and N kanji character
Transmission antenna nodes visible as slight bulges on upper casing
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: STERLING-NAKAMURA EDS-3 laser-etched on left flank; regulatory stamps (GLMZ approved, encryption certification code) on base; serial number engraved into charging port surround
physical_description.condition_typical: Light wear on grip sections from repeated handling; fine scratches on lens cover from document contact; faint heat discoloration around the optical array from sustained use
